newsitem.title: DENMARK: Clinton says NATO trying to save Bosnia peace.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says NATO trying to save Bosnia peace.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton on Friday said the latest drive by NATO to arrest accused Bosnia war criminals was part of an overall attempt to salvage the Dayton peace accords.
"We basically believe that we have to make an effort to save the Dayton process," Clinton told reporters on Air Force One enroute to Denmark from Romania.
British forces on Thursday led raids in their sector of Bosnia that led to the arrest of one suspect. A second person died in a shootout rather than be captured.

Clinton said taking steps to strengthen the efforts of the NATO forces was widely discussed in Madrid at the alliance's summit this week and earlier this month in the United States at a gathering of the seven industrial nations.

"What we admitted to ourselves ... there was too much focus being given to what happens in June of '98 (when the U.S. hopes to withdraw its troops) and too little focus being given to each of these other elements."

Clinton told reporters: "I think it would be a fair conclusion for you to draw that we made a commitment ... that every element should be given greater attention" -- including arms control, helping the infrastructure and economic development.
He said the capture of suspected war criminals "obviously is, at the moment, the most compelling".
